The X AI chatbot Grok made blatantly antisemitic comments right after @ElonMusk touted that it had been “improved”. This is unacceptable and incredibly alarming.

That’s why I joined my colleagues in demanding accountability from X AI. We must not accept this as the new normal for AI. It’s also a warning that AI can carry the biases of its creators, and should be used carefully and within a regulated framework.
Without clear guardrails, there is no reason to believe the behavior of “Grok for Government” in military applications will remain stable or aligned with DoD security and ethics standards.

statements.text:
As AI technology rapidly develops, we must have commonsense guardrails to prevent these influential platforms from generating antisemitic, hateful, or harmful content.

That’s why I’m helping lead a bipartisan resolution that will establish a basis for how AI can be developed responsibly – for the benefit of all Americans.

I'm supporting the GUARDRAILS Act to undo the Trump administrations' one-size-fits-all AI regulation plan, to give states the ability to add commonsense safeguards as artificial intelligence advancements continue to shift the playing field for millions of workers and consumers.

Let me ask you this: will you commit to terminating these partnerships with AI companies when the flagrantly violate basic decency and in the case of the nonconsensual sexual images that Chair Lofgren referenced violate laws?

statements.text:
I represent a community of creators and artists in my district, so I understand exactly how important it is to have control over your own voice and image. With the advancement of AI, we need new laws for new realities.

I’m proud to be an early champion of the NO FAKES Act, a bipartisan and bicameral bill that will give Americans a powerful tool to protect themselves from scammers and bad actors using AI.

The Hollywood unions and workers who make incredible content know first-hand the importance of protecting the creative work of Americans.

I’m proud to echo their voices as an early cosponsor of the NO FAKES Act, which will give Americans – whether they’re an actor or a teacher – a way to protect their identity from those misusing AI to scam, cheat, and steal.

statements.text:
In Hollywood, AI is changing the landscape, threatening the livelihoods of writers, craftspeople, artists, and more. 

If we don’t enact guardrails like the NO FAKES Act, we risk the amazing, original, human-created content that makes film and television so special. 

I raised these issues with the White House’s Science & Tech advisor to ensure this administration works with me to protect irreplaceable human talent.

AI should work FOR Americans, not replace them.

I confronted the White House’s Science & Tech advisor to ensure we’re prioritizing the protection of American jobs.

Listen to a snippet here: https://t.co/vIc4Ji9dqI

We need to make sure that AI doesn’t come at the cost of  American jobs.  And it’s Congress’ responsibility to insure that powerful tech is safe and a net positive.

Take a listen to my full thoughts here:

https://t.co/tRHGL0tSrn

Scams are costing us billions. Congress can pass two bills right now to help Americans avoid getting duped (and I’m an early cosponsor of both).

First, the SCAM Act, a bipartisan bill that will ban paid scam ads and hold social media companies accountable when they profit off of fake advertising. Plus, it gives the FTC, states, and affected consumers the tools they need to hold these companies accountable.

Second, the NO FAKES Act. Too many people are getting scammed by bad actors using AI-generated fakes of loved ones or notable figures. This bill would crack down on this fraud and protect personal identities.

https://t.co/gmlsR0E2zo

statements.text: I’m also a proud cosponsor of the NO FAKES Act, so that AI can’t be used to steal another person’s likeness, voice, or hard work without their consent.
